A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ships/Sahara study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison. Appendices A–E are retained, and v2 adds Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention-head ablation experiments on Llama-2-7b-chat and Vicuna-7b-v1.5, including ASR, helpfulness and appendix experiments on system prompts and course correction.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental outcomes, including Figures 2–6 and the supplementary results in Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same Query/Key or Value scaling interventions, KL-based Ships in Eq. 9, SVD-based generalized Ships and Sahara search in Algorithm 1. The revised preliminary definition and attention-limit formula change the mathematical account without establishing a changed operational procedure.

E1.justification: The harmful-query datasets and prompt, helpfulness and course-correction scenarios are retained. Section 5.3 newly names the benchmarks underlying the existing helpfulness experiment, whose plotted results remain unchanged; this is additional documentation rather than reported added coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain ActSVD, GTAC&DAP, LSP, Masking Head and ACDC. The helpfulness comparison retains SparseGPT and Wanda. Newly cited studies in Appendix F are discussed, not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Table 1 and Section 4.3 revise the reported modification budget from approximately 0.006% to 0.018%, explicitly identifying three heads for the reported 0.72 ASR. This changes the stated comparison setting without establishing that experiments were rerun. Appendix B's input formats, decoding settings and ASR procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The head-count and ablation-type comparisons, head distributions and overlaps, pretrained-attention substitution, helpfulness analysis, system-prompt tests and course-correction analysis are retained. Appendices A and C–E contain no added empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same ± reporting, and the plotted uncertainty displays are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes the proposed method's reported parameter-modification fraction from approximately 0.006% to 0.018%, while retaining ASR 0.72 ± 0.05. The other numerical results and empirical plots, including appendix tables, are unchanged; no same-setting performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: Eq. 5 replaces a refusal-probability difference with KL divergence in the safety-parameter definition. Eq. 7 replaces the scalar uniform-weight expression with a causal lower-triangular averaging matrix, with entries 1/i for j ≤ i and zero otherwise; related Appendix A text is revised. These are localized formal revisions rather than a new theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the Ships/Sahara contributions, the single-head 16-fold ASR claim, safety-feature extraction, overlapping heads across related models and limited helpfulness impact. The Table 1 budget correction does not rewrite these headline claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning feature extraction, parameter redundancy, pretraining and the helpfulness trade-off are retained. Qualifications about excessive ablation producing nonsensical outputs and system prompts introducing in-context-learning effects are also unchanged. Appendix F primarily adds research positioning.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 now explicitly identifies Llama-2-7b-chat and BoolQ, RTE, WinoGrande, ARC Challenge and OpenBookQA for the existing helpfulness evaluation. This improves reproducibility documentation. The generation instructions, hardware/runtime information and code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix F elaborates comparisons with DPO/toxicity attribution, low-rank methods, layer analyses and residual-stream approaches, including criticism of earlier head-ablation methods. New references include Lee et al., Leong et al., an attention-head survey and benchmark sources. This expands context while retaining the existing attention-head-focused positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical and wording edits, updates affiliations and publication headers, and adds acknowledgements and Appendix F. The main section sequence and scientific narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 corrects 'Abalted' to 'Ablated'; the captions incorrectly labelled Figure 5a/5b on page 10 become Figure 6a/6b. Figure 18's text wrapping and box layout change, alongside modest page reflow. No empirical figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting accuracy through the three-head parameter accounting in Table 1 and the causal averaging matrix in Eq. 7. Naming the helpfulness benchmarks improves reproducibility, while Appendix F clarifies research context. These are useful, limited gains with unchanged empirical evidence. Some overstatement remains: Section 4.3 still claims three orders of magnitude despite the corrected comparison of approximately 5% versus 0.018%.
